source.title: Memorization-Dilation: Modeling Neural Collapse Under Label Noise
source.authors: D. Nguyen; R. Levie; Julian Lienen; Gitta Kutyniok; E. Hüllermeier

record.file_problem: Full conference paper text is present; no apparent cutoff affecting the supplied sections.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains networks on corrupted labels and measures test feature collapse and test accuracy against memorization; this is a related measurement of consequences of label noise, not a direct test of whether the networks fit fully random labels as specified in V1–V5. Its results also examine whether training representations of corrupted samples are memorized, bearing conceptually on V6 but not testing the timing or ordering of learning.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that Zhu et al. (2021) studied neural collapse with completely randomized labels, but that is cited prior work and is not this study's result. Its own empirical results are about memorization versus test-feature collapse and test accuracy across label-noise levels and losses. These do not directly measure the claim versions' training-error, optimization-time, unstructured-input, smooth test-error, explicit-regularization, or learning-order outcomes. No result rows qualify for the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study tests the test-error component of V4 in additional architectures and loss settings: Table 2 reports steadily decreasing test accuracy as random-label corruption increases from 0 to 0.3. Missing training-error measurements prevent assessing perfect training fit, but do not make the test-accuracy results irrelevant to V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors characterize neural-collapse optima with nonnegative features and propose an empirically motivated MD model. Under its assumptions, label smoothing yields less memorization and dilation than cross-entropy, offering an explanation for improved generalization. The model is restricted to two classes and omits memorization of clean samples.
record.recipe_differences: The empirical intervention corrupts a fraction of labels and measures penultimate-layer test-feature collapse and test accuracy; it does not reproduce the original random-label fitting experiment. The authors also develop a theoretical model of memorization and dilation.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, number of classes, feature dimension, loss function, label-noise configuration, and architecture vary across experiments. The paper notes that the M=2 binary case sometimes failed to attain the optimal neural-collapse configuration and those cases were filtered out.

fits_no_version.finding: Test-feature dilation approximately tracks the paper's feature-distance memorization metric; CE and LS largely share this correspondence at modest memorization, whereas MSE and LR differ.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the tested noisy-label conditions, feature-space memorization and test-feature dilation covary in a loss-dependent manner.

fits_no_version.finding: Label smoothing generally reduces feature-distance memorization and improves noisy-label test accuracy relative to cross-entropy; the MD model provides a conditional theoretical explanation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Label smoothing can improve generalization under partial label corruption by reducing memorization and dilation.

record.problems: The central empirical measurements are feature-collapse and test-accuracy plots, not direct measures of training-error fitting on random labels. For the binary M=2 experiments, cases that did not attain the optimal neural-collapse configuration were filtered out. The main experiments report ten seeds in the text, while the appendix setting says five runs for assessed parameter combinations; large-scale results use three seeds.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: the paper's own results do not measure the outcomes named by V1–V6. Figures and Table 2 report test-feature collapse or test accuracy, not the relevant training-error, fit-time, input-randomization, regularization-ablation, or learning-order outcomes.

untested.parts: Complete random labeling, zero or near-zero training error, and chance test performance with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time ratios and convergence slowing with increasing corruption; a fixed 200-epoch training budget does not establish either.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit across corruption levels, degradation through complete randomization to chance, and direct evidence that the remaining signal is captured while noise is memorized.
The specified weight-decay, dropout, and augmentation comparisons, including generalization after removing them.
The temporal ordering of learning real patterns and memorizing noisy labels; endpoint feature distances do not establish learning order.

missing.what: Add test-accuracy rows for the corruption sweep, linked to V4's degradation component. The record explicitly excluded these results, but their exclusion rests on the mistaken requirement that training error must also be reported before test accuracy can bear on V4.
missing.locator: Appendix A.2.1–A.2.2, Table 2: all dataset × architecture × CE/LS combinations at η = 0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3; means and standard deviations over three seeds.

record.verdict_notes: No existing rows require correction. The study does not establish V4 in full. Table 2 supports monotonic mean degradation over the tested interval, without establishing statistical significance of every adjacent difference. Its hyperparameters were selected without noise and reused at positive noise levels. Neural-collapse configurations and feature-distance memorization are not substitutes for measured training error.

versions.untested_parts: Whether standard networks fit completely random training labels to zero or near-zero training error with test error at chance, without changing architecture or training hyperparameters.
Relative training time for random versus true labels and convergence time as corruption increases.
Whether the networks fit shuffled, independently permuted, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Whether training error stays perfect and test error rises steadily toward chance as corruption increases; the study measures test accuracy but does not report training error.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent random-label fitting or whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
Whether clean patterns are learned before noisy or random labels, or whether those labels are learned differently over training.

relationships.condition: Test-error degradation over corruption probabilities 0, 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3; ResNet18 and VGG13 with CE and LS on MNIST, FashionMNIST, CIFAR-10, and SVHN.
relationships.reason: Based on the text and Table 2, with no extracted row ids: mean test accuracy decreases at every corruption increment in all 16 architecture–dataset–loss combinations. For example, CIFAR-10 ResNet18 CE decreases from 78.46% to 70.86%, 61.39%, and 52.52%. This supports the measured degradation component.
relationships.display_finding: Mean test accuracy declined at every corruption increment across all 16 combinations, with CIFAR-10 ResNet18 CE falling from 78.46% to 70.86%, 61.39%, and 52.52%.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
